title: sequential-region-evacuation-checklist-and-rollback-benchmarks
creator: Marco Ruiz
description: Goal: Build an automated 'sequential region evacuation' capability for Private (VPC) deployments that can run repeatable failover drills and produce objective rollback/restore benchmarks. This ticket delivers: (1) a Terraform/IaC checklist and module hooks for orderly evacuation, (2) an automation runner that executes preflight checks, traffic-shift, state fencing, and staged rollback, and (3) a benchmark harness which measures RTO/RPO and service-level regression during drills.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform modules expose a single boolean `evacuation_enabled` and staged hook points (preflight, drain, promote, rollback)
Automation runner can run in `dry-run` and `execute` modes and report a pass/fail per stage to the Console dashboard
Health checks (control plane + runtime + state stores) are validated before traffic-shift; if any critical check fails, automation aborts and produces an annotated failure artifact
Automated rollback triggers when error rate or 95th latency crosses configured thresholds during the canary stage
Benchmark run produces an RTO/RPO report and stores artifacts (logs, metrics query links, PR link) to the drill run record
steps: Design Terraform hook interface and update existing private VPC modules to include evacuation lifecycle hooks (PR draft)
Implement automation runner microservice (k8s job) that reads a `drill.yaml` and runs stages: preflight -> drain -> traffic-shift -> canary -> promote -> cleanup/rollback
Add preflight validators: KV lock health, model artifact checksum, epoch metadata sync, DNS propagation stubs
Wire Console integration: drill runner posts stage events and final report to Console API and creates a drill record with links to metrics dashboards
Create benchmark harness that runs synthetic queries, measures token-level latency distributions, and captures throughput loss during transitions
Author runbook and one-click Terraform plan template for on-call engineers to start a rehearsal
comments: 2026-02-26 - Marco Ruiz: Initial scoping completed. Decided to make the runner idempotent and support dry-run mode. Need input from runtime on safe fencing semantics.
2026-03-02 - Priya Shah (runtime): Reviewed preflight validators. KV lock health must also check last-applied-index to detect split-brain. Added note to include clock skew tolerance.

2026-03-05 - Asha Patel: Pushed draft Terraform hooks PR. Using lifecycle hooks named preflight_hook, drain_hook, promote_hook, rollback_hook. Need CI smoke test to ensure modules compile on both AWS and GCP VPC templates.

2026-03-09 - Design (Ellen Park): Reviewed UX for Console drill page. Requesting explicit 'abort' button and a detailed failure log link for each stage. Also suggested tagging runs with customer-id when drills are run against customer-like topology.

2026-03-12 - Asha Patel: Implemented basic canary thresholds; runner will rollback if 5xx rate > 0.5% for 10s or if p95 latency increases > 2x baseline. Logging to the drill artifact bucket is working. Next: add synthetic traffic harness and finalize runbook.

2026-03-12 - Security (Liam O'Connor): FYI - because drills touch private keys for KMS-driven token signing we require an audit entry for each automation-run and a brief security review. Marking `security_review_required` true.
risk_mitigation: Default runs are dry-run; execute mode requires explicit operator approval via Console
All state-changing steps are reversible with deterministic rollback hooks and a tombstone KV fencing pattern
Telemetry gates: automation runner evaluates key metrics and will auto-abort on gap conditions to avoid cascading failures
Sandbox mode available: run the full sequence against a shadow VPC with synthetic workloads before any production drill
